description: Add SQLite as an embedded database option while maintaining PostgreSQL support, eliminating external database dependency for typical users
principles: Rock-solid quality over speed - every feature must be bulletproof before moving on
Comprehensive test coverage - unit tests, integration tests, edge cases
All tests must pass before a story is marked complete
No story is done until it's documented and tested
Backward compatibility - existing PostgreSQL users must not be affected
Fail fast, fail loudly - errors should be obvious and actionable

testingRequirements.coverage: Minimum 90% line coverage for all new code
testingRequirements.unitTests: Every public function/method must have unit tests
testingRequirements.integrationTests: Full workflow tests against SQLite (PostgreSQL optional for comparison)
testingRequirements.edgeCases: Test invalid inputs, missing data, empty tables, migration edge cases
testingRequirements.ci: All tests must pass before story completion
testingRequirements.postgresRequired: PostgreSQL is NOT required for development or testing. All new code must be testable with SQLite only. PostgreSQL comparison tests are optional and skipped when PostgreSQL is unavailable.

fileStructure.description: New database abstraction layer lives in src/python/db/ package

src/python/.config.py: MODIFIED - add get_backend() factory, keep connect() for backward compat
src/python/.cryptoAccounts.py: MODIFIED - use db layer instead of direct psycopg2

db/.backend.py: Abstract DatabaseBackend base class with interface definition
db/.schema.py: DDL for all tables, create_tables() function for each backend

src/scripts/._bootstrap.py: MODIFIED - ensure db package is importable
src/scripts/.(all scripts): UNCHANGED - will work via CryptoAccounts refactor

tests/.conftest.py: NEW - shared fixtures (in-memory SQLite, sample data)

placeholderSyntax.decision: Use named placeholders with dictionary parameters
placeholderSyntax.rationale: Both sqlite3 and psycopg2 support :name syntax with execute(query, {'name': value}). This avoids %s vs ? incompatibility entirely.
placeholderSyntax.note: Existing queries using %s will be converted during SQL-009 refactor

cursorHandling.decision: Backend exposes execute() method that returns list of Row objects
cursorHandling.rationale: Hide cursor complexity inside backend. Callers get results directly.
cursorHandling.interface: backend.execute(query, params) -> List[Row], backend.execute_one(query, params) -> Row|None, backend.execute_scalar(query, params) -> Any

rowType.decision: Query results returned as list of dictionaries
rowType.rationale: Dictionaries are simple, JSON-serializable, and column names are preserved. Both backends can produce these.

nullHandling.decision: Python None is used consistently for NULL/missing values
nullHandling.rationale: Both backends map NULL to None. Query functions return None (not 0) when no data found.
nullHandling.example: get_price() returns None if no price found, not 0.0

timestampFormat.decision: All timestamps stored and returned as ISO 8601 strings in SQLite
timestampFormat.rationale: SQLite has no native datetime. ISO 8601 sorts correctly and is human-readable.
timestampFormat.note: PostgresBackend converts datetime objects to strings for consistency

transactionSemantics.decision: Explicit commit required for write operations
transactionSemantics.rationale: Both backends will use explicit transaction control. No autocommit.

errorHandling.decision: Backend raises DatabaseError for all database-related failures
errorHandling.rationale: Unified exception type simplifies error handling in calling code

cliScripts.description: Complete list of CLI scripts requiring verification in SQL-011

SQLite DDL uses: REAL for floating point (FLOAT8, NUMERIC, DOUBLE PRECISION)
SQLite DDL uses: TEXT for timestamps (stored as ISO 8601: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS')

Unit tests: parent directory creation

userStories.title: Port get_price() and get_price_date() functions to Python
acceptanceCriteria: Create db/queries/price.py with PriceLookup class
Constructor takes DatabaseBackend instance
get_price(from_coin: str, to_coin: str = 'USD', price_date: str = None) -> float | None
get_price_date(from_coin: str, to_coin: str = 'USD', price_date: str = None) -> str | None
price_date parameter is ISO 8601 string; defaults to current date if None
Matching algorithm (must match PostgreSQL function exactly):
1. Filter pair_price where from_curr = from_coin AND to_curr = to_coin
2. Filter to same calendar day (year, month, day match)
3. If multiple matches, select the one with smallest minute-difference from price_date
4. Return price (or date) from that row, or None if no matches
Return None (not 0.0) when no price found
Use single SQL query with ORDER BY and LIMIT 1 (no Python sorting)
SQL query must work identically on SQLite and PostgreSQL (use strftime for date parts)
Unit tests with in-memory SQLite:
- Exact timestamp match returns correct price
- Same-day fuzzy match returns closest price by minute
- No match on day returns None
- Multiple prices same day returns closest to requested time
- Empty pair_price table returns None
userStories.notes: Critical function. Test thoroughly. The SQL must use strftime() which works on both backends.

userStories.title: Port get_balance() and get_sum_of_all_transfers() to Python
acceptanceCriteria: Create db/queries/balance.py with BalanceCalculator class
Constructor takes DatabaseBackend instance
get_balance(coin: str) -> float:
- Returns SUM(buy where buy_curr=coin) - SUM(sell where sell_curr=coin)
- Excludes trans_type = 'Stake' from buy sum (matches PostgreSQL function)
- Returns 0.0 if no transactions (not None)
get_sum_of_all_transfers(coin: str) -> float:
- Same calculation but only includes trans_type IN ('Withdrawal', 'Deposit')
- Returns 0.0 if no transfers
SQL uses COALESCE to handle NULL sums: COALESCE(SUM(...), 0)
Unit tests:
- Balance with only buys
- Balance with buys and sells
- Balance excluding stakes
- Zero balance (no transactions)
- Negative balance (sold more than bought)
- Transfer sum with mixed transaction types
userStories.notes: Simple functions. Return 0.0 (not None) for empty results - this matches how balances should work.

userStories.title: Port get_trades() to Python
acceptanceCriteria: Create db/queries/trades.py with TradeQuery class
Constructor takes DatabaseBackend instance
get_trades(coin: str) -> List[dict]:
- Returns list of trade dictionaries, ordered by date ascending
- Each dict has keys: date, to_curr, to_quantity, price, from_curr, from_quantity
- Filters: trans_type = 'Trade' AND (buy_curr = coin OR sell_curr = coin)
- to_quantity is positive for buys, negative for sells (relative to coin parameter)
- price is calculated as: counter_amount / coin_amount
- Uses CASE expressions matching the PostgreSQL function exactly
Returns empty list [] if no trades (not None)
Unit tests:
- Buy trade (USD -> BTC): to_quantity positive
- Sell trade (BTC -> USD): to_quantity negative
- Multiple trades ordered by date
- No trades returns empty list
- Trades for different coins don't appear
userStories.notes: The CASE logic determines buy vs sell perspective. Match PostgreSQL exactly.

userStories.title: Port get_trade_cost_new() to Python
acceptanceCriteria: Add get_trade_cost(coin: str, cost_currency: str = 'USD') -> List[dict] to TradeQuery class
Returns list of trade dictionaries with cost basis information
Each dict has keys: date, curr, quantity, trade_curr, trade_quantity, cost_curr, unit_cost, total_cost, cost_curr_quote_date
For each trade from get_trades():
- If trade was in cost_currency (e.g., USD): unit_cost = trade price directly
- If trade was in other currency: unit_cost = trade_amount * get_price(trade_curr, cost_currency, date)
- total_cost = unit_cost * abs(quantity)
- cost_curr_quote_date = date used for price lookup (from get_price_date or trade date if direct)
If get_price() returns None for a cross-currency trade, set unit_cost and total_cost to None
Inject PriceLookup dependency via constructor: TradeQuery(backend, price_lookup=None)
Unit tests:
- Trade in USD: direct cost, no price lookup needed
- Trade in EUR: requires price lookup EUR->USD
- Trade with missing price: unit_cost and total_cost are None
- Multiple trades with mixed currencies
userStories.notes: Depends on SQL-003 (PriceLookup) and builds on SQL-005 (get_trades). Use dependency injection for testability.

userStories.title: Port get_avg_purchase_price_new() to Python
acceptanceCriteria: Create db/queries/basis.py with BasisCalculator class
Constructor takes TradeQuery instance (dependency injection)
get_avg_purchase_price(coin: str, cost_currency: str = 'USD') -> float | None:
- Gets trade costs from TradeQuery.get_trade_cost(coin, cost_currency)
- Filters to purchases only: quantity > 0
- Calculates: SUM(unit_cost * quantity) / SUM(quantity)
- Returns None if no purchases exist (not 0.0)
- Returns None if all purchases have None unit_cost (missing prices)
- Skips trades with None unit_cost in calculation (partial data is okay)
Unit tests:
- Single purchase: returns that price
- Multiple purchases: returns weighted average
- No purchases (only sales): returns None
- Mix of purchases with and without price data: calculates from available
- All purchases missing price data: returns None
userStories.notes: Returns None for no-data cases. Calling code must handle None appropriately.

userStories.title: PostgreSQL to SQLite data migration tool
acceptanceCriteria: Create db/migration.py with migrate_postgres_to_sqlite(pg_backend, sqlite_path) function
Create src/scripts/migrate_to_sqlite CLI script
Migration process:
1. Connect to PostgreSQL using existing credentials (PGHOST, etc.)
2. Create new SQLite database at target path
3. For each table (ledger, pair_price, coins, wallets): SELECT all rows, INSERT into SQLite
4. Convert PostgreSQL timestamps to ISO 8601 strings during transfer
5. Report row counts for each table
6. Verify: row count in SQLite matches PostgreSQL for each table
Dry-run mode (--dry-run flag): connect, count rows, report what would be migrated, don't write
Target path: --output flag or default to ~/.cryptoaccounting/ledger.db
Error handling:
- If target file exists, abort with error (don't overwrite). Use --force to override.
- If migration fails mid-way, delete partial SQLite file and report error
- Wrap entire migration in transaction, rollback on any error
Skip migration if PostgreSQL is empty (0 rows in ledger) - warn user
Unit tests: timestamp conversion, row counting logic
Integration test: migrate sample data, verify queries return same results
userStories.notes: Requires PostgreSQL access. Skip tests with pytest.mark.skipif when PGHOST not set.
